description: Synthetic BigQuery-shaped query pairs. Labels are the authors' reading of BigQuery semantics, not yet confirmed on the emulator.

tables.orders: CREATE TABLE orders AS SELECT * FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 'a' AS customer, NUMERIC '10.50' AS amount, TIMESTAMP '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00' AS ts, ['x','y'] AS tags, STRUCT('Oslo' AS city, '0150' AS zip) AS addr), STRUCT(2, 'a', NUMERIC '20.00', TIMESTAMP '2024-01-02 00:00:00+00', ['y'], STRUCT('Oslo', '0150')), STRUCT(3, 'b', CAST(NULL AS NUMERIC), TIMESTAMP '2024-01-02 00:00:00+00', CAST([] AS ARRAY<STRING>), STRUCT('Bergen', '5003')), STRUCT(4, 'b', NUMERIC '5.00', TIMESTAMP '2024-01-02 00:00:00+00', ['z'], STRUCT('Bergen', '5003'))])
tables.target: CREATE TABLE target AS SELECT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-02 00:00:00+00' AS ts
tables.t1: CREATE TABLE t1 AS SELECT x FROM UNNEST([1, 2, 3]) AS x
tables.t2: CREATE TABLE t2 AS SELECT y FROM UNNEST([1, CAST(NULL AS INT64)]) AS y
tables.nums: CREATE TABLE nums AS SELECT n FROM UNNEST([NUMERIC '0.1', NUMERIC '0.2']) AS n

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: SELECT id, customer, amount FROM orders QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY ts DESC, id) = 1
cases.right: SELECT id, customer, amount FROM (SELECT id, customer, amount, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY ts DESC, id) AS rn FROM orders) WHERE rn = 1

cases.label: not_equivalent
cases.left: SELECT id, customer FROM orders QUALIFY RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY ts DESC) = 1
cases.right: SELECT id, customer FROM orders QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer ORDER BY ts DESC, id) = 1
cases.note: needs a tie on ts within a customer: customer b has one

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: WITH big AS (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount > 6), named AS (SELECT id, customer FROM big) SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n FROM named GROUP BY customer
cases.right: SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n FROM (SELECT id, customer FROM (SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount > 6)) GROUP BY customer

cases.label: not_equivalent
cases.left: SELECT id, tag FROM orders CROSS JOIN UNNEST(tags) AS tag
cases.right: SELECT id, tag FROM orders LEFT JOIN UNNEST(tags) AS tag
cases.note: needs a row with an empty array: id 3

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: SELECT id, tag FROM orders, UNNEST(tags) AS tag
cases.right: SELECT id, tag FROM orders CROSS JOIN UNNEST(tags) AS tag

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: SELECT addr.city AS city, addr.zip AS zip FROM orders
cases.right: SELECT t.addr.city AS city, t.addr.zip AS zip FROM orders AS t

cases.label: equivalent
cases.right: SELECT STRUCT(addr.city AS city, addr.zip AS zip) AS addr FROM orders

cases.label: not_equivalent
cases.left: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE ts > (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM target)
cases.right: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE ts >= (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM target)
cases.note: needs a row whose ts equals the target's max

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer
cases.right: SELECT customer, COUNT(1) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer

cases.label: not_equivalent
cases.left: SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer
cases.right: SELECT customer, COUNT(amount) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer

cases.label: not_equivalent
cases.left: SELECT x FROM t1 WHERE x NOT IN (SELECT y FROM t2)
cases.right: SELECT x FROM t1 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t2 WHERE t2.y = t1.x)
cases.note: NOT IN over a NULL returns no rows

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: SELECT id, IFNULL(amount, 0) AS a FROM orders
cases.right: SELECT id, COALESCE(amount, 0) AS a FROM orders

cases.label: not_equivalent
cases.left: SELECT -id AS id FROM orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
cases.right: SELECT -id AS id FROM orders ORDER BY orders.id LIMIT 1
cases.note: BigQuery reads the alias in ORDER BY (checked on real BigQuery in an earlier thread); a name-resolution trap

cases.label: equivalent
cases.left: SELECT n FROM nums WHERE n = 0.1
cases.right: SELECT n FROM nums WHERE n = NUMERIC '0.1'
cases.note: a decimal literal next to a NUMERIC column becomes NUMERIC in BigQuery (checked on real BigQuery in an earlier thread); a fidelity trap for the emulator
